newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says net reserves doubled in April.
newsitem.headline: Russia says net reserves doubled in April.

text.p: Russia's net international reserves doubled to 23.5 trillion roubles on May 1 from 11.3 trillion on April 1 mainly because of central bank currency purchases, a senior Central Bank official said on Tuesday.

"This rise is due to our purchases on the domestic market," First Deputy Chairman Sergei Aleksashenko told Reuters. "We are buying currency on the market... We bought in February, March, April and May." The central bank reserves this year are calculated at a rate of 5,560 roubles to the dollar, against a current trading level of about 5,780 to the dollar.

Aleksashenko noted that the International Monetary Fund disbursed a 500 million SDR ($700 million) quarterly tranche from its three-year loan to Russia at the beginning of May. Money from the loan does not appear in net reserves, but is available to the central bank for intervention.

The Finance Ministry used this money for current spending, so that roubles came on to the market, surprising many banks, as the rouble had been strong for most of the month. As a result many banks started buying dollars recently.

"Banks which have invested in dollars in the last few days are making a mistake from our point of view. The abundance of roubles on the market is not a trend, but a short-term current situation. And this situation obviously will re-occur every three months, when the IMF tranche arrives," he said.
